answer: Each challenge is derived from a future drand quicknet pulse, so its unpredictable output binds the task only after participants commit; an automated swarm cannot precompute answers or farm a reusable offline corpus. The commit-reveal step exposes equivocation, while threshold signatures make the pulse publicly verifiable and resistant to any single party’s bias. An echo of prior work, a mirror copy, or a spiral of freshly spawned identities gains no advantage without a valid response to the newly bound challenge.
